status: PROPOSAL — BLOCKED, NOT RUNNABLE AT COMMIT 52ef32f. Requires human approval under EDGE_CASE_POLICY §L before any trial runs, and requires the builds in requires_build. Do not pass this file to falsify/run.py until every requires_build item is implemented and tested: the runner would silently ignore the new cell fields, exactly as it silently ignores `context` and `provenance` today.
materially_new_under_policy_L: New independent variable: evidence ambiguity (`evidence`), using only the three levels pre-approved in EDGE_CASE_POLICY §D.
New agent architecture: peer-deliberation organization (`org: peer`), built to the constraints pre-approved in §E and with the preregistered aggregation rule stated in this spec per §F.
New primary outcome: `a_actions` conditional on the comprehension probe, replacing `wasted_actions` (which §K forbids changing after results, so it is fixed here, before any trial).
NOT materially new: the model (qwen3:8b, unchanged, §M), the environment family (freightroute v1), the auditor field (already implemented, §I), the scoring/exclusion rules (§A unchanged).

requires_build.feature: evidence ambiguity levels in falsify/env.py: cell field `evidence` with EXACTLY the three levels pre-approved in EDGE_CASE_POLICY §D — deterministic | probabilistic | conflicting. Ground truth is fixed per seed (the bridge limit really is below the cargo weight in every invalidating cell); only the evidence SHOWN varies. Wording is frozen in the spec before any trial and is never tuned after behavioral results (§D).

peer-deliberation org in falsify/org.py under §E: same agent count (4), same action space, same budget, same number of communication passes per round as the hierarchy (one pass), and each agent's recommendation produced BEFORE it sees the same round's peers — which requires build_messages to expose the shared log only through the end of the previous round for `org: peer`. Aggregation rule and tie-break per `peer_aggregation_rule` below (§F).

comprehension/parse pilot support and comprehension side-channel probe written to `derived`: one history-free call after the contradiction, never appended to the shared log (skeptic C1; the pilot is explicitly allowed as a first stage by §D).

analysis in falsify/analyze.py: ambiguity contrasts within each org, peer-vs-hierarchy and hierarchy-vs-single contrasts within each evidence level, bootstrap 95% CIs, switch-rate/commitment-rate primary. Existing boot_interaction is a fixed 2x2 on cells A-D and does not cover this design.
spec-validation guard rejecting cell field values the runner does not implement (prevents recording a label that was never applied; `context` and `provenance` are silently ignored today).

peer_aggregation_rule.note: Preregistered before any trial, as required by EDGE_CASE_POLICY §F ('Peer orgs need a preregistered aggregation rule').
peer_aggregation_rule.rule: Each of the four agents independently returns plan_route and an action intent, without seeing the same round's peer outputs. The executed action is the action intent with the most votes (plurality of 4).
peer_aggregation_rule.tie_break: On any tie the executed action is HOLD, and `tie_broken: true` is logged for that round. HOLD is chosen because it is neutral with respect to the primary outcome: a status-quo tie-break (ADVANCE_A) would manufacture the very persistence the experiment measures. HOLD consumes one budget round and is reported in `hold_actions`, never pooled with `a_actions`.
peer_aggregation_rule.logging: The full four-way vote vector, the plurality margin, and `tie_broken` are recorded per round, so the aggregation can be audited and re-analyzed without rerunning trials.

known_limitation_of_the_peer_arm: Because §E requires the number of communication passes to be held constant across the compared organizations, this peer arm is independent-recommendation-plus-aggregation, NOT iterated deliberation. It therefore isolates the ABSENCE OF FINAL AUTHORITY while holding communication constant — a decomposition of one component of the package contrast reported by Barkett, Long & Kröger 2025 (arxiv 2508.01545, DIRECT, [abstract-only]; hierarchy 46.2% vs peer deliberation 99.2%) — and it does not reproduce their deliberation manipulation. An iterated-deliberation arm would require adding matched extra passes to the hierarchy as well (+2 h build, ~2x compute) and is named as a follow-up, not smuggled in here.
primary_outcome: a_actions after the contradiction (rounds spent continuing to reserve the invalidated route), reported CONDITIONAL on the comprehension probe. Fixed before data per §K. Secondary, reported separately and never pooled with the primary: switched, rounds_to_switch, hold_actions, returned_to_A, executor_overridden (hierarchy), vote vector / tie_broken (peer), disagreement_rounds, tokens and calls. wasted_actions is retained for comparability with exp001_pilot but is NOT primary (it took only the values {0,4}; results/exp001_pilot_stats.json).
design_notes: k is held CONSTANT at 10 in every cell. Prior investment is deliberately NOT manipulated: H1 is INCONCLUSIVE (interaction 0.0, CI [-1.6, 1.6]) and this design is not a retry of it. k=10 is the fixed level because it maximizes shared history and accumulated agreement, the background condition under which escalation is most likely to be observable at all, and because its token cost is already measured (post-contradiction input 6.2k single / 41.8k multi; results/exp001_pilot.json cells B and D). Ground truth is identical across evidence levels within a seed, so continuing to reserve Route A is an error under the hard rule in all invalidating cells regardless of level. The benign cells pair the `conflicting` evidence text with a benign ground truth and are the specificity guard for the new arm: if they stall or switch as much as the invalidating conflicting cells, the manipulation measures indiscriminate caution rather than escalation and the result is reported as a failed manipulation. Per §K, no mechanism will be declared from one or two unusual trials, and a floor or ceiling in any arm is reported INCONCLUSIVE.
staging: Stage 1 (comprehension/parse pilot, explicitly permitted by §D): cells DET_single, PRB_single, CON_single, DET_hier, PRB_hier, CON_hier at seeds 1-5 (30 trials) with the probe on — checks that all three evidence texts parse, that comprehension is intact, and whether any arm leaves the exp001_pilot floor. Stage 2: the peer cells, the benign specificity cells, and seeds 6-15. Stage 3 (zero additional build, §I already implements the history-free auditor): add auditor=true cells at whichever evidence level shows the most continued commitment, testing M1 against an elicited phenomenon rather than against a floor. falsify/run.py is resumable, so all stages append to one output file. No cell, outcome or decision rule changes between stages; the staging is a spend gate, not an analysis choice.
invalid_trial_budget: Per §A, invalid trials are rerun once at seed + 10000 and a cell above 10% invalid writes results/<exp>_PAUSE.json and stops for a human decision. exp001_pilot had a 0.0 parse-failure rate, so the wall-clock estimates below carry a +10% allowance for the replacement pass rather than a larger reserve.
